target_customer: Egyptian businesses and platforms that embed loans and accounts for their gig workers and micro-business customers
problem: Gig workers and micro-businesses in Egypt are unbanked and cannot get credit; platforms want to offer advances against earnings.
business_model: lending and virtual accounts via API (interest/fees on loans repaid from earnings)
product_category: Embedded finance / lending for gig workers

founders.name: Omar Ekram
education: American University in Cairo and Columbia University, BA Economics and Finance (CFA)

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring, loan servicing and API integration for a new market, with regulatory and collections complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded integration with platforms and repayment from earnings flows create some lock-in; no licence moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger Egyptian lenders and fintechs were scaling consumer credit; no source shows any incumbent copying or buying Dayra.

market_need_then: 2021 coverage describes large unbanked gig and micro-business populations in Egypt; reported loans of $100-$2,500 repaid from earnings and company-claimed growth above 50% per month (unverified).

brand_strength.rationale: Short name, but only funding coverage and no brand-specific evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Dayra raised a reported $3M pre-seed (debt and equity) in March 2021 from Egyptian and YC backers and a founder with private equity and banking background, and is listed Active. No news after 2021 was found, so later traction, rounds and any stall cannot be assessed; the record shows an early-stage fintech with local funding and no verified later outcome.
notes: Funding verified across Wamda, Crowdfund Insider and others for the 2021 pre-seed only. CB Insights lists $6.15M over 7 rounds including a Nov 2022 round attributed to Hub71; unverified, not recorded. No dated 2020-2021 competitor source was found (later articles name MNT-Halan, Paymob, valU and Khazna, but are dated 2024-2026); list left empty. Site fetch returned only the word Dayra.
